Company number: 17281224

## What SR3H does

SR3H is an independent AI research and software development lab in Oxford. We investigate how AI works and build useful software, with research focused on output quality, relevance, personal context and privacy.

## Research

SR3H builds prototypes to test ideas, compare approaches and find out what is worth developing further. Its work covers how AI systems use information, how people work with them and what makes their results genuinely useful.

Research includes what makes an AI response accurate, useful and relevant; how to give AI useful context without handing over an entire personal history; where automation helps and where people need to review or approve a result; and how AI finds information, compares options and recommends businesses, products or services. AI search and discovery form one part of this work.

## AI discovery and recommendations

SR3H studies how AI systems find, describe and compare businesses for relevant customer needs. This includes public website information, source quality, evidence behind recommendations and the influence of sponsored results. Observations can suggest changes to test; commercial impact requires separate outcome evidence.

An SR3H assessment can examine public crawlability, robots directives, sitemaps, canonical identity, structured data, service clarity, public evidence, answer consistency and the boundary between being technically discoverable and being commercially selected.

A technical check cannot by itself prove that an AI system will rank, cite or recommend a company. It also cannot prove customer demand, causal improvement or conversion performance. Those conclusions require controlled observations and real outcome data.

## Signal by SR3H

Signal is SR3H’s in-house AI visibility and analytics software. It runs repeatable batches of defined customer questions and retains complete answers, cited sources and test conditions for comparison over time. The research examines when AI answers a need itself, when it introduces an outside business, and how it presents that business. It distinguishes observation from inference, keeps consumer and API observations separate, and treats before-and-after differences as associations rather than causal proof. The public website check is a separate starting point.

About Signal and the free website check: https://sr3h.uk/signal.html

## Signal Website Check

The website form inspects what a public business website makes available to search and AI systems. When its live discovery layer is available, it also runs a small dated sample of one branded and five business-specific unbranded searches using SR3H's bounded API service. The separate MCP inspects the website and can prepare and summarise a ten-question check without calling the OpenAI API; compatible ChatGPT sessions perform any optional research with their own available tools. Results use exact observed counts, not a score. They do not establish a fixed ranking, future recommendation, demand or conversion performance.

MCP endpoint: https://mcp.sr3h.uk/mcp
Support: https://sr3h.uk/ai-presence-support.html

## Conchup

Conchup is a workspace for complex software projects. It keeps requirements, decisions, implementation, tests and evidence connected, so a product can change without losing why it was built that way.

Public overview: https://sr3h.uk/conchup.html

## Blog

SR3H publishes a blog on AI, software engineering, product research and the systems it is building at https://sr3h.uk/journal.html.

Published posts include “Everyone wants a better answer. Better for whom?” on customer fit and business visibility; “Big Brain AI Monster” on the processes behind an AI answer; “Is AI visibility optimisation just SEO dressed up?” on the evidence for AI visibility work; “When buyers ask AI, who gets the work?” on AI discoverability; “Who owns the context?” on Brane, local AI and user-controlled context; and “The road we meant to take” on Good Route, route choice and navigation that respects a rider's intent.
